title: The Effect of Optimized Perception of Loudness on Speech Comprehension in the Presence of Background Noise
summary:
The study aims to address the complex interrelationship between speech understanding and loudness perception. When fitting hearing aids, it is crucial to adjust the amplification so that optimal speech understanding is achieved without unduly increasing perceived loudness in everyday situations. To date, hearing aid fitting has often been viewed as a
trade-off between these two goals, since increasing amplification to optimize speech understanding often leads to many everyday sounds becoming too loud, which can impair patient acceptance of the hearing aid fitting. Current fitting procedures, such as NAL-NL2, are based on statistical averages and do not sufficiently account for individual loudness perception. People with hearing loss who have similar tone audiograms
require very different amplification levels—which can vary by up to 30 dB in some cases—to achieve compensation through hearing aid fitting that brings their loudness perception close to normal levels.  Therefore, this study examines whether a loudness-validated fine-tuning of the standardized fitting—following an initial setting using NAL-NL2—can lead to better results in terms of speech understanding in noise.

interventions.name:
Administration of the Oldenburg Sentence Test (OLSA)  [1 hour]
        Program 1 selected:
       2 training lists, each with 20 sentences, at a high initial SNR (+10 dB).
        1 test list with 30 sentences.
        Change of hearing program (P1 → P2)
        1 test list with 30 sentences.

Conducting the Oldenburg Sentence Test (OLSA)  [1 hour]

        Program 2 selected:
        2 training lists with 20 sentences at a high starting SNR (+10 dB).
        1 test list with 30 sentences.
        Change of hearing program (P2→P1).
        1 test list with 30 sentences.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Minimum age of 18 years.
Sufficient knowledge of German to understand the participant information and instructions and to be able to complete the Oldenburg Sentence Test.
Tone audiometric hearing loss at at least two frequencies (from 500 Hz, 1 kHz, 2 kHz, 4 kHz; 4PTA) greater than 30 dB HL.
Difference between bone conduction and air conduction at the PTA frequencies must not exceed 15 dB.

Tone audiogram profile:

No low-frequency hearing loss with normal hearing thresholds in the high-frequency range and a sloping hearing loss toward the low frequencies,
no mid-frequency dips,
no asymmetric hearing loss with a tone audiometric hearing threshold difference in the PTA of more than 20 dB,
No steep high-frequency drops (normal hearing in the low-frequency range, hearing loss of more than 65 dB HL above 500 Hz).

Additional requirements:

External auditory canals clear, no cerumen impaction.
No evidence of retrocochlear hearing loss.
Maximum discrimination score on the Freiburg Speech Test of 50% or better.
No hearing loss bordering on deafness (WHO 4-criterion met)
Exclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria not met
